title: Lean and cvc5 show as native binaries with no lifecycle, though sandbox ships them as toolchains
foundBy: repository owner: "The dashboard isn't reporting Lean as a toolchain, with its lifecycle etc, in the deps dashboard", and "CVC5 should count as a toolchain as well"

evidence.verified: `make check` passed on the tree that became c8ad176, with 191 tests. `make dependencies` then wrote sandbox's Lean 4.34.1 and cvc5 1.4.2 as runtime records, each with phase `recent`, no `eol` and `policy` `none`. Lean's two newest lines were 4.35 and 4.34, and its status was minor behind 4.35.0 at level info. elan stayed a native record. Headless Chrome screenshots of the lifecycle view showed both rows under Toolchains and runtimes, in the light and the dark theme. A copy of the data with Lean on a superseded line drew the bar striped after `window_end`, with the warning chip.

resolution: Lean and cvc5 are toolchains with no end of life, because neither publishes a support window. Their lifecycle rows say whether the pinned line is one of the two newest.
details:
sandbox's image/Containerfile.base installs the Lean toolchain and the cvc5 solver from their GitHub releases, each pinned by an `ARG *_VERSION`. `upstream_from_url` in collector/extract.py turns only Temurin, Go, Node.js and Maven downloads into a `runtime` record. Any other GitHub release download becomes a `native` record. So the dependencies page lists both as native binaries, outside "Toolchains and runtimes", and gives neither a lifecycle.

A lifecycle comes from endoflife.date, which has no product for either, or from a publisher's own policy. Neither project publishes a support window or a long-term line.

Wanted: both are toolchains, with no end of life, because neither publishes one. The lifecycle calendar still shows whether a pin's line is one of the two newest, from the GitHub releases. elan stays a native binary beside nvm and pyenv.
